paraphrase: Laugh, play, keep meditation; day and night speak the knowledge of Brahman; those who laugh and play yet do not break the mind abide ever steady with the Nāth.
notes: Not available locally; the saying is recalled from the Gorakh Bānī (Baṛthvāl) without its number, so the ref is section-level with a running suffix. Wording not quoted.
speaker: Gorakhnāth (ascribed)

paraphrase: Die, O yogī, die — death is sweet; die that death by which Gorakh died and saw.

paraphrase: In the circle of the sky is an upside-down well where the nectar dwells; one who has a guru drinks it to the full, one without a guru goes away thirsty.

paraphrase: Eating, one dies; not eating, one dies: Gorakh says, son, one crosses over by restraint (saṃjam) alone; dwell always in the middle.
